title: Multiple Linear Regression I
description: Study the foundations of multiple linear regression: least squares estimation, interpretation, model assumptions, goodness of fit, inference for individual coefficients, partial regression, binary variables, transformations, and interactions. Complete the source exercises; exercises requiring the referenced empirical datasets state the required method because those datasets are not included in this source.

questions.question: What quantity is minimized to obtain the least squares regression plane with \(k\) explanatory variables?
questions.answer:
The least squares estimates minimize the sum of squared residuals:
\[
SS(b_0^*,\ldots,b_k^*)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left[y_i-\left(b_0^*+b_1^*x_{i1}+\cdots+b_k^*x_{ik}ight)ight]^2.
\]

questions.question: State the normal equations and the least squares estimator when \(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}\) is invertible.
questions.answer:
The normal equations are
\[
\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{y}.
\]
If \(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}\) is invertible, the unique least squares estimator is
\[
\mathbf{b}=(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{y}.
\]

questions.question: In the regression function \(\mathrm{E}y=\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\cdots+\beta_kx_k\), how is \(\beta_j\) interpreted for a continuous explanatory variable?
questions.answer:
\( eta_j\) is the expected change in \(y\) per one-unit change in \(x_j\), holding all other explanatory variables fixed. Equivalently,
\[
 eta_j= rac{\partial}{\partial x_j}\mathrm{E}y.
\]

questions.question: What does a coefficient on \(\ln x\) mean in a model with \(\ln y\) as the response?
questions.answer:
In a log-log model, the coefficient is an elasticity: it is approximately the percentage change in \(y\) associated with a 1% change in \(x\), holding other variables fixed. Mathematically,
\[
 rac{\partial\ln y}{\partial\ln x}=\left( rac{\partial y}{y}ight) igg/\left( rac{\partial x}{x}ight).
\]

questions.question: Under assumptions F1--F4, what are the expectation and variance of the least squares estimator \(\mathbf{b}\)? What additional conclusion follows under F5?
questions.answer:
Under F1--F4,
\[
\mathrm{E}\mathbf{b}= oldsymbol{ eta},\qquad
\mathrm{Var}(\mathbf{b})=\sigma^2(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}.
\]
Thus, \(\mathbf{b}\) is unbiased. Under F1--F5, \(\mathbf{b}\) is normally distributed.

questions.question: Define the mean square error and residual standard deviation in a regression with \(k\) explanatory variables.
questions.answer:
With residuals \(e_i=y_i-\widehat y_i\),
\[
s^2=MSE= rac{1}{n-(k+1)}\sum_{i=1}^n e_i^2,
\qquad
s=\sqrt{ rac{1}{n-(k+1)}\sum_{i=1}^n e_i^2}.
\]
The quantity \(s\) is also called the standard error of the estimate.

questions.question: Give the total-variation decomposition, \(R^2\), and adjusted \(R^2\) for multiple linear regression.
questions.answer:
The decomposition is
\[
\mathrm{Total\ SS}=\mathrm{Error\ SS}+\mathrm{Regression\ SS}.
\]
The coefficient of determination is
\[
R^2= rac{\mathrm{Regression\ SS}}{\mathrm{Total\ SS}}.
\]
The adjusted coefficient is
\[
R_a^2=1- rac{(\mathrm{Error\ SS})/[n-(k+1)]}{(\mathrm{Total\ SS})/(n-1)}=1- rac{s^2}{s_y^2}.
\]

questions.question: How is a two-sided \(t\)-test conducted for \(H_0:\beta_j=0\)?
questions.answer:
Compute
\[
t(b_j)= rac{b_j}{se(b_j)},
\]
where
\[
se(b_j)=s\sqrt{	ext{the }(j+1)	ext{st diagonal element of }(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}}.
\]
At significance level \(\alpha\), reject \(H_0\) if
\[
|t(b_j)|>t_{n-(k+1),1-\alpha/2}.
\]
For large samples, a common 5% rule of thumb is \(|t|>2\).

questions.question: How can the partial correlation between \(y\) and \(x_j\), controlling for all other explanatory variables, be computed from the coefficient \(t\)-ratio?
questions.answer:
Use
\[
r(y,x_j\mid x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1},x_{j+1},\ldots,x_k)
= rac{t(b_j)}{\sqrt{t(b_j)^2+n-(k+1)}}.
\]
It is the correlation between residuals from the two regressions used to form the added variable plot.

questions.question: For \(\mathrm{E}y=\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\beta_2x_2+\beta_3x_1x_2\), what is the marginal effect of \(x_1\), and why is this an interaction?
questions.answer:
The marginal effect is
\[
 rac{\partial\mathrm{E}y}{\partial x_1}= eta_1+ eta_3x_2.
\]
It is an interaction because the effect of \(x_1\) changes with the value of \(x_2\).

questions.answer:
The numerical coefficients and medians are unavailable. For GROUP \(=0\), the GPWCOMM interaction is zero, so use the main coefficient \(b_{\mathrm{LNGPWCOMM}}\). At group-0 medians \(G_0\) and \(E_0\),
\[
\Delta\mathrm{EXPENSES}\approx b_{\mathrm{LNGPWCOMM}} rac{1+E_0}{1+G_0}
\]
for a \(\$1\) increase in GPWCOMM.

questions.question: National Life Expectancies: Interpret the coefficient associated with health expenditures without using the logarithmic expenditure scale.
questions.answer:
The numerical coefficient is unavailable. If the fitted model includes \(b_{\ln H}\ln(H)\), where \(H=\mathrm{PRIVATEHEALTH}\), then a small percentage increase in health expenditure has an expected LIFEEXP change of approximately
\[
b_{\ln H}	imes	ext{the proportional change in }H.
\]
For example, a 1% increase in \(H\) is associated with an approximate change of \(0.01b_{\ln H}\) years in LIFEEXP, holding FERTILITY and PUBLICEDUCATION fixed.

questions.question: National Life Expectancies: Is PUBLICEDUCATION statistically significant? State the hypotheses, decision criterion, and decision rule.
questions.answer:
The fitted output is unavailable, so significance cannot be numerically determined. Test
\[
H_0: eta_{\mathrm{PUBLICEDUCATION}}=0,
\qquad H_a: eta_{\mathrm{PUBLICEDUCATION}}
e0.
\]
Compute
\[
t= rac{b_{\mathrm{PUBLICEDUCATION}}}{se(b_{\mathrm{PUBLICEDUCATION}})}.
\]
At level \(\alpha\), reject \(H_0\) when \(|t|>t_{n-(3+1),1-\alpha/2}\), using the sample size \(n\) of the fitted model.

questions.answer: An added variable plot shows the relationship between a response and one explanatory variable after controlling for other explanatory variables. questions.question: National Life Expectancies: Calculate the correlation corresponding to the added variable plot in Figure 3.11.
questions.answer:
A numerical calculation requires the PUBLICEDUCATION coefficient \(t\)-ratio and sample size from the fitted model, neither of which is given in the source excerpt. Calculate the plot's partial correlation as
\[
r(\mathrm{LIFEEXP},\mathrm{PUBLICEDUCATION}\mid\mathrm{FERTILITY},\ln\mathrm{HEALTH})
= rac{t(b_{\mathrm{PUBLICEDUCATION}})}{\sqrt{t(b_{\mathrm{PUBLICEDUCATION}})^2+n-(3+1)}}.
\]
Equivalently, compute the ordinary correlation between the two sets of plotted residuals.
